title: Family and being a paid 'dummy' in parade bands
summary: His musical side comes from his mother's family; cousin Johnny Peugeot got him into parade bands where he filled out the numbers without playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: background was mostly from my, uh, uh, mother's side.

See, I, I had a cousin, uh, that played music. He was a clarinet player. His name was Johnny Peugeot. And, uh, he played with, uh, Papa Lane's band and, uh, Uses band. We used to call it Puckeye Uses band. We used to call it Puckeye Uses band. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. And, uh. We used to call it Puck Iuse's band. A fellow with Glass Eye used to play cornet. And played with Fish's band in those days. He was the one who got me started in playing the band, you know, because they used to book parades. They'd have about ten men in a band. They would have six men playing and four of us was dummies. And I was one of the dummies. It started like that with a rag in my heart. I couldn't play though, but I got paid anyhow to fill the band out. In those days, that's the way they did it.
To get you started. What did your cousin say? They'd have ten men and there'd be four niggers, five dummies?

Yeah. Yeah, you see. Excuse me. He used to tell me that. He would say they had folk calling people in a plane. I said, well, I turn around and look. I said, well, I surely don't see anybody around here. Look, she called it. He said, well, they got four of them in here playing. And they'd point them out to me afterwards, you know. But I was green as grass, man. I was a big time. Boy, I thought, man, playing in that band, boy, I was something big. You know, just starting out in a band like Fisher's Band. And there was bands in Lane's Band. There was a few other bands in them days. Triangle. And, uh, oh, I tell you, man, I played with so many bands. I played with this, uh, well, I played with, uh, Chink Martinet and, uh, Paul Lionel, Elysian Field and Dauphin. It was right above the police station. I can't think of that. Near the Lusitania? Yeah, the Lusitania Hall, yeah.
